check.name: RightCurlyOfExpression
check.description:
Checks the placement of right curly braces ('}') for expression blocks: array initializers, block-bodied lambda expressions and anonymous classes.

The right curly brace of an expression block is different from the right curly brace of a code block, because it is always followed by another part of the expression or the statement, for example a semicolon, a closing parenthesis or a method call. For this reason the policies of this check are defined by the position of the right curly brace in relation to the previous part of the expression, and not in relation to the part that follows it. Placement of right curly braces for code blocks is validated by RightCurly check.

It is possible to enforce three different policies:

  • on_same_line - The right curly brace must be on the same line as the previous part of the expression: 
    
 String[] names = new String[] {"One", "Two", };
 Runnable action = () -> { doSomething(); };
  • on_new_line - The right curly brace must be on a new line: 
    
 String[] names = new String[] {"One", "Two",
 };
 Runnable action = () -> { doSomething();
 };
  • on_new_line_or_singleline - The right curly brace must be on a new line, unless the whole expression block is on a single line: 
    
 // Single-line format of block
 String[] names = new String[] {"One", "Two", };

 // Multi-line format of block
 String[] names = new String[] {"One", "Two",
 };

For multi-dimensional arrays only the outer right curly brace is validated. For anonymous classes only the right curly brace of the class body is validated, the right curly brace of an instance initializer inside such class is not an expression brace and is not validated.

property.name: option
property.description: Specify the policy on placement of a right curly brace ('}') of an expression block.
